mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate below 0.5% compresses discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as capital costs decline.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS remains below 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Payroll growth exceeding 0.5% month-over-month signals robust corporate hiring and earnings momentum, generating positive S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of months with PAYEMS growth above 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate rise above 4.0% triggers monetary tightening that increases equity discount rates, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts falling below 850.0 thousand units indicate weakening consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of months with HOUST below 850.0.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous industrial production decline below 90 and retail sales drop below 400,000 million dollars signals supply chain contraction, causing negative S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO < 90 and RSAFS < 400000.

mechanism_narrative: High employment (PAYEMS > 132,000) combined with elevated unemployment (UNRATE > 13.0%) indicates labor market stress that reduces consumer spending, producing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS > 132000 and UNRATE > 13.0.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion regimes (GDPC1 > 18,000 and HOUST > 850.0), strong GDP growth and housing momentum drive positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when GDPC1 > 18000 and HOUST > 850.0.

mechanism_narrative: High-inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 250 and FEDFUNDS >= 0.05) trigger aggressive rate hikes that reduce equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 250 and FEDFUNDS >= 0.05.
